q: How much electricity and CO2 does pumping groundwater from a borewell take per kilolitre?
title: Borewell pumping energy and CO2 per kL
short: kWh per kL = 9.81 x total head in metres / (3,600 x pump and motor efficiency). Lifting water 50 m at 40 percent efficiency takes about 0.34 kWh per kL, or about 0.24 kg CO2 per kL at India's grid factor of 0.710. Deeper water and worn pumps raise it.
audience: Factories and campuses on borewell water

p: Lifting 1 kL (1,000 kg) of water by 1 m takes 1,000 x 9.81 = 9,810 joules, or 0.002725 kWh. Multiply by the total head and divide by the wire-to-water efficiency of the pump and motor together.

sections.h: Total head is more than the borewell depth
ul: Pumping water level: the level while the pump runs, below the resting level because of drawdown.
Delivery height: from ground up to the overhead tank inlet.
Friction in the rising main and pipes, often a few metres; more in long or narrow pipes.

p: Submersible pump sets lose energy in the motor, the pump and the cable. A worn or oversized set can fall below 40 percent wire-to-water. Measure it from input kW against flow and head, or ask an energy auditor. A correctly sized, efficient set can reach well above that, which cuts kWh per kL in proportion.

ol: Fit a flow meter on the borewell outlet if there is none.
Read the pump's energy sub-meter and the flow meter at the start and end of a week.
kWh per kL = kWh used / kL pumped; multiply by 0.710 for kg CO2 per kL.
Repeat in summer, when the water table drops and head rises.

example.title: Worked example: a campus pumping 100 kL a day
lines: Total head: 60 m pumping level + 15 m to the tank + 5 m friction = 80 m; pump set efficiency 40 percent
Per year: 54.5 x 365 = 19,893 kWh and 14,124 kg CO2, about 14.1 t
A new set at 55 percent: 0.002725 x 80 / 0.55 = 0.396 kWh per kL, 27 percent less
example.note: Head and efficiency are assumptions; use your own levels and measured efficiency.

senseible: Senseible reads your electricity bills, and two readings of a pump sub-meter in a photo give the units as their difference, with the CEA factor of 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh applied. Water volumes come from your own flow meter.
